newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram takes oath as cabinet minister.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram takes oath as cabinet minister.

text.p: P. Chidambaram on Thursday took the oath of office as a cabinet minister in Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 11-day-old government.

Earlier, government officials said Chidambaram, whose regional party decided on Tuesday to join the government, would enter the new centre-left cabinet as finance minister and pilot the 1997/98 (April-March) budget through parliament.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma inducted Chidambaram, M. Arunachalam and Jaipal Reddy into the government as full cabinet ministers.
Three others were sworn in as junior ministers -- Maqbool Dar, S.R. Balasubramaniam and Dhanushkodi Athithan.

Their portfolios would be announced later, but Arunachalam was expected to return to government as labour minister, while Balasubramaniam would be junior personnel minister and Athithan junior human resource development minister.

Chidambaram, Arunachalam, Balasubramaniam and Athithan all belong to the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party, which tentatively decided to stay out of the government on April 19 but reversed its stand on Tuesday. The TMC is the third largest component of Gujral's United Front coalition.
